Testing Additivity of Lead and Benzo[a]pyrene–induced Neurotoxicity in Caenorhabditis elegans Assays

Niccolò Anceschi

1 Overview

This document reproduces the main results for the BaP–Pb drug additivity analysis from the manuscript Anceschi, Huayta, Meyer, Dunson and Herring, (2026+) “Testing Additivity of Lead and Benzo[a]pyrene–induced Neurotoxicity in Assays”. It loads the pre-processed C. elegans assay data, fits the single-drug margins and the joint radial-spline surface, and producess figures for the dose-response surfaces and log-likelihood comparisons reported in the paper. Each section below sources one script from the pipeline, in dependency order. Each sourced script contains dedicated and detailed documentation of its contents.

The convex-mixture model employed represents every ordinal damage-score distribution as \((1-\lambda)F_0 + \lambda F_\infty\), interpolating between an unexposed and a maximal-effect profile. The dose dependence enters entirely through the weight \(\lambda(\cdot)\), a monotone non-decreasing function that governs the whole outcome distribution. Under joint exposure, it becomes a surface \(\lambda_{12}(d_1,d_2)\) over the dose plane. Additivity is tested by a likelihood ratio comparing the fitted joint model against different nulls – Bliss, Loewe\(^+\), and Hand – each inducing an additive baseline surface \(\lambda_{12}^{(o)}\) built from the single-drug fits.

2 Configuration

When this document is opened in RStudio, the repository path is detected automatically from the file’s location, so no manual editing is needed. data_file names the pre-processed data expected alongside the scripts.

source_dir <- dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path) # repo local path 
data_file <- "C-elgans_preprocessed_data.rds" # pre-processed data file

3 Utilities

Load required packages and define generic helpers (softmax, mixture probabilities, monotone inversion by root-finding).

source(file.path(source_dir, "Utils.R"))

4 Data import and setup

Import the pre-processed assay data and build everything that does not depend on the fitted parameters: the single- and joint-exposure spline bases, the dose constants and spline dimensions, the extremal-profile PMFs, and nested exposure data subsets.

source(file.path(source_dir, "Data_setup.R"))

5 Likelihoods and radial splines

Define the likelihood functions — both for single and joint exposures — and the penalized radial-spline objective — together with the caching helpers that keep each optimizer step cheap.

source(file.path(source_dir, "Loglikelihood.R"))

6 Additive null models

Define the three additive baselines \(\lambda_{12}^{(o)}(d_1,d_2)\) — Bliss, Loewe\(^+\) (EME), and Hand — using spline parameters to be fitted on single-exposure data.

source(file.path(source_dir, "Null_models.R"))

7 Model fit

Fit the two stages: first the single-exposure behavior for both BaP and Pb, then the joint-exposure surface via radial-splines under a monotonicity penalty. This is the computational core; the timing messages from tic()/toc() report each fit.

source(file.path(source_dir, "Model_fit.R"))
## Fit Single-Exposure Data: 3.003 sec elapsed
## Fit Joint-Exposure Data: 15.676 sec elapsed

8 Result Visualization

Produce the fitted weight-function plots, the joint weight-surface contours for each null and for the radial fit, the fitted-vs-empirical CDF scatterplots, and the across-subset log-likelihood comparison.

source(file.path(source_dir, "Plots.R"))

Single-drug weight functions and the Pb→BaP dose alignment.

plot_weight_functions(save = FALSE)

Joint weight surfaces: the three additive nulls and the radial fit.

plot_weight_surfaces(save = FALSE)

Log-likelihood across data subsets and models.

plot_loglik(save = FALSE)

Fitted vs. empirical CDFs, all data and joint exposures only.

plot_cdf_scatter(save = FALSE)

9 Bootstrap Test for Additivity

The additivity tests are calibrated by a parametric conditional bootstrap: for each null model, replicate datasets of the joint exposures data are drawn from the corresponding additive baseline, the radial surface is refitted on each, and the likelihood-ratio statistic is recomputed to build its null distribution – from which p-values and power are obtained.

Refitting the model on every replicate is computationally intensive: the analysis in the manuscript used 10,000 replicates per hypothesis and was run in parallel across multiple nodes on a computing cluster.

For transparency and completeness, the full procedure – replicate simulation, aggregation, and computation of the test statistics, p-values, and power – is provided in Bootstrap_test.R.
